On mobile the controls fill more than a full screen before the table starts, and model names and the metric value are clipped at 375px, so collapsible filters might be worth suggesting.

I'm noting that the mobile table cuts off the metric values at first view, so the ranks show with nothing to explain them, and I could suggest a narrower Compare column or a sticky rank and model column. The tabs wrap awkwardly on mobile, and the minimum label matches select sits detached from its label, both minor issues.

I'm noting that the mono secondary text, like "nebius/fp4 · high reasoning" and "complete", is small and low in contrast, and the tiny metric eyebrow is hard to read. The rows are tall enough that only about five fit at 1440, and the stacked complete-calls cell drives that height, so it could be laid out inline to give more density.

I'm noting that the scroll cue at 1440 may be misleading if the table actually fits, so I'd hedge and suggest hiding it when there's no overflow. The superscript footnotes on the complete-calls and known-USD headers point to text I can't see in these screenshots, so I'll treat that as a limitation. Command A+'s 17 of 18 complete calls and its tie at rank 1 are consistent with the operations view showing 12 eligible configurations.

I'm finishing the export and header notes, and I'm noting the export buttons don't say whether they cover the current filtered view. The ranked metric column has no marker in the header, and the operations heading reads clearly. I'm now weighing whether any of this is a release blocker or just fixes to make before shipping.

I'm weighing whether the ranked-metric visibility problem rises to a release blocker. The scores look like they clear the bar, and the user can still scroll to reach the column, so I'm leaning toward treating it as the top-priority fix rather than a hard stop.

I'm settling on a verdict now: no hard release blockers, since the scores clear the bar, but the clipped ranking metric at 1440 is a high-priority fix before wider circulation. I'm being upfront that I can only judge what's visible in the screenshots, not how the interactions behave.
